title: Impinj M750 UHF Inlay — Authenticated RAIN RFID for Brand Protection and Retail Privacy
summary: The Impinj M750 (Monza R6-P silicon class) is the brand-protection variant of the M700 family — adding 32 bits of User memory plus full EPC Gen2 v2 Untraceable, Authenticate and Crypto Suite 3 (AES-128) support on top of the M730's baseline retail platform. Proud Tek supplies M750 inlays for cryptographic anti-counterfeit programs, retail privacy at point-of-sale (Untraceable command), pharmaceutical serialization where on-tag User data is required, and the EU Digital Product Passport UHF tier.
heroPoints: Cryptographic Authenticate (AES-128). Chip-level challenge–response proves the silicon is genuine Impinj R6-P, not relabelled lower-grade chip. Foundation for any UHF brand-protection program; pairs with Impinj's Authenticity cloud service for turnkey verification without operating your own HSM.

EPC Gen2 v2 Untraceable — at point-of-sale or on-exit, the chip can be commanded to return a shortened EPC, hide its TID and hide User memory until the next power cycle. The standard implementation pattern for retail privacy under GDPR-aware deployments.

32-bit User memory. Sufficient for compact serialization data (batch ID, expiration date offset, encrypted serial fragment, DPP URL hash). Step up to NXP UCODE 9 if you need 224-bit User; step down to M730 if you need none.

sections.title: Where the M750 is the right engineering choice
bullets: Mid-market brand protection. Cryptographic anti-counterfeit at UHF range without the silicon-ASP step up to NXP UCODE DNA. The M750 + Impinj Authenticity service combination removes the need for the brand owner to operate their own HSM/KMS, making cryptographic UHF authentication deployable in months rather than quarters.

Retail privacy at point-of-sale. The EPC Gen2 v2 Untraceable command lets a POS reader send a single shortened-EPC instruction at checkout. Subsequent reads outside the store return a 32-bit shortened EPC that cannot be tracked back to the SKU. Standard pattern for GDPR-aware EU retail rollouts.

EU Digital Product Passport UHF tier. DPP guidance for UHF supports User memory holding the DPP URL pointer plus chip-level Authenticate to prove the carrier is genuine (anti-substitution). The M750's 32-bit User + Authenticate combination is the minimum-feature DPP-compliant UHF chip; UCODE 9 is the alternative when more User memory is needed.

Pharmaceutical serialization with on-tag fragments. DSCSA / EU FMD encoded data primarily lives in a backend keyed by EPC, but on-tag User memory can hold a tamper-evident expiration-date offset or a partial encrypted serial that lets a receiving warehouse validate before backend round-trip. M750's 32 bits is sufficient for a 4-byte timestamp offset.

Returnable transit items requiring cycle authentication. RTI tagging benefits from periodic Authenticate verification to detect counterfeit RTI insertion. M750's Authenticate command runs in <50 ms per tag and integrates cleanly into pallet-portal inventory cycles.

sections.title: When NOT to choose the M750
bullets: Pure SGTIN-96 retail volume tagging. The M750's silicon ASP is roughly 30-40% higher than the M730. If the application does not actually use Authenticate, Untraceable or User memory, the M730 is the correct cost-optimized choice.

Maximum sensitivity / longest read range. The M750 trades ~0.6 dB of read sensitivity (−22.0 vs M730 −22.6 dBm) for the additional feature circuitry. Where every dB of range matters (small-antenna, on-metal extreme), the Alien Higgs-9 (−24.0 dBm) or NXP UCODE 9 (−23.0 dBm) may be a better fit.
Sensor or moisture-detection applications. No sensor variant exists in the M750 line. UCODE 9xe is the choice for moisture/temperature sensing.

Bank-grade per-message signing (e.g. luxury goods anti-counterfeit). M750 Authenticate is a chip-authenticity primitive, not a per-message signature. For per-message AES-128 signing with read-counter binding (the UHF analogue of NTAG424 DNA SUN messages), step up to NXP UCODE DNA. The M750 + Impinj Authenticity is suited to mainstream brand protection where 'cryptographic but not bank-grade' is sufficient.

sections.title: Impinj Authenticity service integration
bullets: Impinj ships M750 chips with pre-loaded per-chip cryptographic keys registered to Impinj's Authenticity cloud service. The brand owner does not need to provision keys, run an HSM, or maintain a key-management service.

Verification pattern: a reader (fixed, handheld or smartphone via NFC tunnel) issues an Authenticate challenge; the chip responds with a CMAC-style proof; the reader posts the proof to the Authenticity cloud REST API; the API returns 'authentic' / 'not authentic' / 'unknown' in <200 ms typical.

Brand-owner integration cost: a single REST API integration plus a UI flow on the verifier side. No on-premise key infrastructure. Typical proof-of-concept to production rollout is 4-6 weeks for a brand with an existing reader fleet.

Alternative: brand-owner-managed keys with the Impinj Crypto Suite 3 (AES-128). For high-value applications where the brand owner requires custody of the verification key. Higher integration cost but no third-party in the trust chain.

Counterfeit defense: Impinj Authenticity rejects any chip that did not ship from an Impinj wafer with a registered key. Relabelled M730 silicon (the most common counterfeit pattern) is rejected because the chip cannot produce a valid CMAC response.

faq.question: Is the Impinj M750 the same as the Monza R6-P?
faq.answer: Yes — Impinj rebranded the Monza R6-P silicon as the M750 as part of the M700-series naming refresh. Datasheets, EPC Gen2 v2 feature support and TID prefix are unchanged. Existing readers, encoders and inlays branded as Monza R6-P interoperate with M750 inlays.

faq.question: How does the M750 differ from the NXP UCODE 9?
faq.answer: Both implement the EPC Gen2 v2 Untraceable + Authenticate + Crypto Suite 3 feature set. Differences: the UCODE 9 has more configurable User memory (32-224 bits vs M750's fixed 32 bits), supports Hide-EPC (the M750 does not), and offers the Self-Adjust auto-detune feature (vs Impinj Autotune). The M750 has the Impinj Authenticity cloud service available out-of-the-box; UCODE 9 deployments either operate their own KMS or use a third-party. Choose by inlay supplier preference and whether you need >32 bits of User memory.

faq.question: Can I use the M750 with my existing Impinj reader fleet for Authenticate?
faq.answer: Yes. EPC Gen2 v2 Authenticate is supported by Impinj R700-series and R420-series fixed readers and the IPJ-R0510 handheld with current firmware (Octane / xArray Octane). If your reader fleet predates 2018 you may need a firmware update to access Authenticate; basic read/write of M750 EPC works on any standards-compliant reader without changes.

faq.question: What is the silicon ASP premium of M750 versus M730?
faq.answer: Indicative pricing at 1M pieces: M730 ~US$0.018, M750 ~US$0.024 — roughly a 30% premium for Authenticate + Untraceable + 32-bit User memory. At 10M+ pieces the premium narrows. For applications that genuinely need any of the three added features the premium is well worth it; for pure SGTIN-96 retail volume the M730 is the right choice.

faq.question: Does the M750 support the EU Digital Product Passport (DPP)?
faq.answer: Yes — the M750 meets the minimum-feature UHF DPP profile: 32-bit User memory holds the DPP URL pointer or hash, Authenticate proves the chip is genuine (anti-substitution) and EPC Gen2 v2 compliance ensures global reader interoperability. For DPP profiles requiring larger on-tag data (full DPP URL plus serial plus sustainability fields), step up to NXP UCODE 9 with 224-bit configurable User memory.

faq.question: What MOQ does Proud Tek offer for M750 inlays?
faq.answer: 10,000 pieces for stock antenna designs. The slightly longer 4-6 week lead time (vs M730's 3-4 weeks) reflects Authenticate-key provisioning at the chip level. For Impinj Authenticity service integration we coordinate the registration step on the brand owner's behalf as part of the first production batch.
